raw_case_text:
During the 2016 ZIKV outbreak in Merida, Mexico, a 27-year-old woman in the third trimester of pregnancy was referred to medical geneticist because multiple malformations detected in the fetus. Informed consent was obtained for sampling, clinical evaluations, and for the publication report. Exploring the medical records, she reported unquantified fever, preauricular nodes, pruritus and rash in the shoulder girdle and thorax in the first trimester when the pregnancy was unnoticed. No serological tests were performed for ZIKV at that time. Ultrasound was performed at 16.4 weeks of gestation with report of fetal growth within normal ranges; but at 23 weeks of gestation, the fetal hands were not identified. At 27.4 weeks of gestation, fetus was reported with microcephaly (DBP 58 mm); nuchal thickening, ventriculomegaly, hemisphere hypoplasia and cerebellar vermis were detected in the brain, and micrognathia, right radial aplasia, and arthrogryposis were also reported at that time.
A stillbirth with generalized subcutaneous edema was obtained via cesarean section at 35 weeks of gestation. At physical exploration showed craniofacial disproportion, microcephaly, irregular anterior and lower posterior hairline. Posterior sloping of the forehead and hypertelorism were observed. The nasal bridge, the nostrils and the filtrum were normal. Retrognathia and normal oral cavity were found. The ears were cupped with low implantation and thickened helix. The shoulders were short, with internal rotation and presented limitation to abduction. The left upper limb presented an extended elbow with limitation to the reduction, pronation arm, flexed wrist, non-reducible hand with cyanotic coloration. The upper right limb was conformed only to the proximal third of the arm. At this level, soft tissue defect was found with the presence of an irregular cutaneous line, exposure of subcutaneous tissue and the humeral condyle, no tissue bleeding was detected (Figure 1). The lower extremities presented limitation to hip abduction, knee extension and flexion of both feet. The genitalia anatomy showed 1 cm penis and a complete rough scrotum without testes inside.
On the skull x-ray, everted sutures and partial collapse of the cranial bones with a hypoplastic occipital was observed. The radiograph of the upper extremities shows a right humerus shorter than the left, with preserved of the distal region of the humerus (Figure 2). Computational axial tomography reported subcortical calcifications, lissencephaly, ventriculomegaly, and generalized cortical degeneration. The karyotype was normal, 46, XY. The serological test for toxoplasma, rubella, cytomegalovirus and herpes virus were negative in the mother and the patient. The RT-PCR for ZIKV/Dengue/Chikungunya in the patient's cerebrospinal fluid detected the presence of Zika viral RNA. Autopsy was not authorized.

subjective.chief_complaint: A 27-year-old pregnant woman in Merida, Mexico, was referred in the third trimester during the 2016 Zika virus outbreak for multiple severe fetal central nervous system and limb malformations detected on prenatal ultrasonography.
subjective.history_of_present_illness: During the first trimester, prior to recognizing her pregnancy, the patient experienced an acute illness with unquantified fever, preauricular lymphadenopathy, pruritus, and a rash over her shoulder girdle and thorax. While an initial prenatal ultrasound at 16.4 weeks of gestation showed normal fetal growth, a follow-up ultrasound at 23 weeks failed to visualize the fetal hands, and ultrasonography at 27.4 weeks identified severe microcephaly, brain malformations, right radial aplasia, and arthrogryposis, leading to genetic referral and cesarean delivery of a stillborn male fetus at 35 weeks of gestation.
subjective.past_medical_history: Resident of Merida, Mexico, during the 2016 Zika virus outbreak.
subjective.review_of_systems: Maternal first-trimester history positive for fever, preauricular lymph node swelling, pruritus, and shoulder girdle/thoracic rash.

objective.physical_examination: Male stillbirth delivered via cesarean section at 35 weeks of gestation exhibited generalized subcutaneous edema, severe microcephaly with craniofacial disproportion, irregular anterior and low posterior hairlines, posterior sloping forehead, hypertelorism, retrognathia, low-set cupped ears with thickened helices, and normal nasal bridge, nostrils, philtrum, and oral cavity. Musculoskeletal and extremity examination revealed short internally rotated shoulders with limited abduction; left upper limb arthrogryposis with an extended elbow, pronated forearm, flexed wrist, and non-reducible cyanotic hand; severe transverse terminal reduction defect of the right upper limb truncated at the proximal third of the arm with an irregular cutaneous border and exposed subcutaneous tissue and humeral condyle without bleeding; bilateral lower limb arthrogryposis with limited hip abduction, limited knee extension, and bilateral foot flexion contractures; and a 1-cm penis with a rugated empty scrotum (bilateral cryptorchidism).
objective.routine_investigations: Fetal ultrasound at 16.4 weeks of gestation was normal; ultrasound at 23 weeks showed non-visualization of the fetal hands; ultrasound at 27.4 weeks showed microcephaly (biparietal diameter 58 mm), nuchal thickening, ventriculomegaly, cerebral hemisphere and cerebellar vermis hypoplasia, micrognathia, right radial aplasia, and arthrogryposis. Postmortem skull radiograph demonstrated everted cranial sutures, partial collapse of the cranial vault bones, and occipital bone hypoplasia; upper extremity radiographs showed a shortened right humerus with preservation of the distal humeral condyle and absence of the forearm and hand.
objective.advanced_workup: Postmortem head computed tomography (CT) demonstrated subcortical calcifications, lissencephaly, ventriculomegaly, and generalized cortical degeneration. Fetal karyotype was normal male (46,XY).

assessment_and_plan.assessment_and_confirmation: Final diagnosis: Congenital Zika Syndrome (microcephaly, lissencephaly, subcortical calcifications, ventriculomegaly, and arthrogryposis) complicated by a severe right upper limb transverse terminal reduction defect and stillbirth at 35 weeks of gestation. Real-time RT-PCR of fetal cerebrospinal fluid (CSF) was positive for Zika virus RNA and negative for dengue and chikungunya viruses, while maternal and fetal TORCH serologies (Toxoplasma gondii, rubella virus, cytomegalovirus, and herpes simplex virus) were negative. Formal autopsy was declined by the family.
